correctness.rationale: The integer identity 2(P_s(x)-P_s(y))=(x-y)((s-2)(x+y)-(s-4)) is valid for all x,y. If s=2 mod4 the difference has an odd multiplier and is injective mod 2^k. If s=0 mod4, completing a square with odd coefficient gives the standard square-root multiplicities; the zero/odd valuation and k=1,2 edge cases have been checked. For odd s, same-parity collision impossible, while opposite parity collision forces x+y=2m+1-2r, where r=(s-2)^(-1) mod m; disjoint pairs count d=min(r-1,m+1-r), yielding d holes/d doubles. Independent enumeration tested s=3..80,k=1..8, corroborating the proof, not exhausting parameters.
residual_risks: Finite independent computations are corroboration only; proof needs all parameter quantifiers and regularity hypotheses.
